rationale: Objective: minimize max-rank summed NCCL kernel duration (max over ranks of the per-rank median of 3 separately profiled runs; original baseline 38.09/38.40 ms) subject to step_ms <= 121.95 ms (1.05x 116.14). Repair of the concrete previous failure: trial-98426ff10f(-param-7e7d0495) selected the two c10d::allreduce_ functional sites, was bitwise exact (max_abs_error 0.0 over 248,879,617 elements, 2 continuous steps), fully covered (12+1 reference invocations), and its alignment logic measurably worked (rank-0 communication median 38.09 -> 36.59 even in that run), yet failed only the step_ms constraint (214.67 > 121.95). The binding_cost AB/BA collector on this exact parent revision (observations/previous-after/binding_cost-2087a4f7.json) isolates the cause as the binding layer, not the candidate: parent arm median step_ms 115.7/119.3 ms vs binding-only passthrough arm 217.0/226.3 ms, i.e. the legacy functional dispatch mode (TorchDispatchMode active around the whole run, ~7,240 dispatcher-visible ops per step) adds ~97-107 ms to ANY functional-site bundle before candidate code runs, and the scoped backend cannot resolve those sites (site_parent is the non-module project.invoke boundary 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0). So the repair is to keep the validated rendezvous mechanism but host it on a module boundary, which uses a direct callable boundary with zero functional sites (binding-contract.md) and per-call overhead of only 4 Python invocations per step. Why the metric has recoverable headroom on this revision (measured): the transfer floor at the exact observed sizes is ~34.5-35.1 ms (collective_calibration-1af5837f: median 1.993 ms per 28,351,488 B x12 and 10.61-10.65 ms per 157,541,376 B; LL=SIMPLE within noise, transport-bound SHM/PCIe pair, peer_access 0, no NVLink), and the current-revision nsys capture shows a fully tight train at that floor (rank 0: 11x~1.96 + 3.10 + 10.45 = 35.13 ms) while the baseline median is 38.09-38.40; the ~3-3.9 ms difference is in-kernel spin-wait. Where the wait comes from (measured on this revision, execution_timeline-1221e205 cross_rank, CPU-only alignment bounds): rank 0 submits every bucket allreduce 5.2-6.4 ms before rank 1 (spread 6.15-6.42 ms at sequence 21 decaying only to 5.23-5.50 ms at sequence 33), so rank 0's first kernel runs 8114 us = 6.2 ms wait + 1.93 ms transfer and later kernels still wait ~0.5-0.75 ms each; the separate nsys run shows the same structure in extreme form on the other rank (leader's first kernel 205.7 ms spin, all remaining kernels at floor). The offset is created across the whole step, not inside the reduction phase: per-microbatch grad_ready timestamps show the cross-rank lag growing 2.98 -> 2.54 -> 5.19 -> 5.35 ms at the end of backward for microbatches 1-4. Selected boundary: module group b57f55423ea79f2933a2 (torch.nn.modules.linear.Linear, target gpt2.lm_head, call 03e8e3a0a8a549d528e18317, phase microbatch_forward_backward, 4 invocations per step, parent call e0792f081096ebc6d62f90ed). It is the last module invocation of every microbatch forward, i.e. the latest forward-side rendezvous point before each loss/backward; for microbatch 4 it lands only ~1-3 ms of host work before the reduction train starts (bucket 0 contains the head-end parameters h.11+ln_f per communication-ownership.json, so it is the first allreduced bucket). lm_head is bound at instance level (the 48 distinct Conv1D groups show instance-level binding), so the evaluator's separate serial-reference model is untouched and no rank-asymmetric barrier is possible; both ranks execute the identical 4 invocations per step, so barrier counts are symmetric by construction. The replacement is parent-exact passthrough plus one gloo barrier on the adapter's existing state['control'] group (created in prepare, already used by before_run outside timing; opop_adapter.py:156-170,191-196): no tensor, collective argument, stream or gradient semantic is touched, outputs are bitwise identical, the barrier launches no NCCL/CUDA kernel so it adds nothing to the kernel-duration sum, and no workload constant is embedded (the barrier fires on every invocation). Rejected with measured cause: re-selecting the c10d functional sites or any functional bundle (repeats the +97-107 ms dispatch failure under legacy backend); NCCL_PROTO/ALGO forcing (trial-3ca928eb87: kernels remained RING_LL and calibration shows SIMPLE gains nothing at these sizes); reducing communicated bytes (the atol=0/rtol=0 exact replica check plus grad tolerance 1e-6/1e-4 forbid lossy reduction of the 497,759,232 B fp32 payload); changing bucket layout (DDP is constructed with bucket_cap_mb=25 in the frozen prepare; not reachable from a module boundary and risks gradient_as_bucket_view aliasing); replacing NCCL with another backend (request fixes distributed_backend=nccl and communication is required). A single group is the coherent editable boundary: one edit, no dependency on other edits, so joint scope is unnecessary. Per the single-group contract, affected_calls contains exactly the selected group's replaced call 03e8e3a0a8a549d528e18317; the two c10d::allreduce_ calls d0938de87369efd500322679 (12x 28,351,488 B) and b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b (1x 157,541,376 B) are not replaced, not enclosed by this boundary and therefore not listed - they are only the observed calls whose kernel durations (the metric) the proposal intends to change, which is descriptive context, not an edit.
hypothesis: Replacing the gpt2.lm_head module boundary with parent-exact passthrough followed by one gloo barrier on state['control'] (4 symmetric rendezvous per step, one right after each microbatch's vocabulary projection, before loss/backward) moves the cross-rank submission skew out of NCCL kernel durations. The microbatch-4 barrier lands after the last module call of the final forward, ~1-3 ms of host work before bucket 0 is submitted, and the earlier barriers cap lead growth at about one microbatch; since the observed 5.2-6.4 ms submit offset is accumulated across the whole step (grad_ready lag 2.98->5.35 ms over microbatches 1-4) and the leader's first kernel absorbs essentially the entire offset as spin-wait (8114 us = 6.2 wait + 1.93 transfer; nsys leader extreme 205.7 ms first kernel with the remaining 12 kernels at floor), aligning before the reduction phase should drop the leader's first kernel from ~8.1 ms toward the ~2.0 ms transfer time and collapse the residual ~0.5-0.75 ms per-bucket waits, giving a max-rank median objective of ~35.1-36.5 ms versus the 38.09-38.40 baseline (~1.6-3.0 ms, 4-8%), bounded below by the measured ~34.5-35.1 ms floor. step_ms should stay ~flat: the laggard that defines the max-rank wall passes the barrier immediately, the leader exchanges host-barrier wait for kernel wait it no longer pays, four gloo barriers cost ~0.1-0.3 ms host each, and with zero functional sites there is no TorchDispatchMode to repeat the measured +97-107 ms failure, leaving the 5.8 ms constraint headroom intact. Correctness is structural: bitwise-identical logits and gradients (no tensor or collective semantics modified), so the exact replica check, serial-reference gradient/parameter checks, finite-loss check, and phase/coverage requirements (4 module invocations inside every adapter.run invocation, including warmup, repeats, continuous steps, the 3 profiled diagnostic runs and the inventory-hook run) are unaffected. Explicit unknowns, to be tested: (a) the clean/profiled skew is sampled at n=3 per rank (waiter excess 2.9-6.8 ms); if the measured runs draw the low end the gain shrinks toward ~1-2 ms, and a run with near-zero natural skew gains little beyond variance capping; (b) residual drift over loss+backward-to-bucket-0 (~0.3-1 ms in the profiled regime) and per-bucket submit jitter remain unremoved, so the floor will not be exactly reached; (c) gloo barrier exit jitter may leave 0.1-0.5 ms of wait inside the first kernel; (d) leadership flips between runs (baseline rank-1 sample 42.69; nsys rank-1 238.93) - the barrier is symmetric and caps whichever rank leads, but a rank-role flip between the barrier and the train start would leave a partial wait on the new leader; (e) the module binding's per-call overhead is assumed negligible at 4 calls/step but the measured step_ms and binding_cost receipt must confirm no unexpected dispatch-mode activation.
